channel.title: Updated · all tabs
channel.description: Daily news and research, explained: every tab

item.title: Regulators close Indiana's United Fidelity Bank, the largest US bank failure since April 2024
item.description: The OCC closed United Fidelity Bank, a $5.9 billion lender based in Evansville, Indiana; First Citizens took over most deposits and assets, and the FDIC expects a $1.83 billion cost. (FDIC, FDIC Failed Bank List, Newsweek)

item.title: Wall Street closes its best week in more than a year as the S&P 500 gains 5.6%
item.description: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% on Friday and 5.6% over a holiday-shortened week, its best since April 2025, one week after falling into a correction. (KSL (AP), Global News (AP))

item.title: US goods trade deficit widens to $149.5 billion in October as AI equipment lifts imports to a record
item.description: The US goods deficit jumped 10.7% to $149.5 billion in October as imports reached a record $365.3 billion, led by capital goods tied to the AI buildout. (US Census Bureau, The Globe and Mail (Reuters))

item.title: Ottawa unveils a first national forestry strategy backed by $6.5 billion to move the industry beyond lumber and pulp
item.description: Canada's government set out a forestry strategy to 2050 with $6.5 billion for new plants, mill upgrades and wood supply, aiming to cut reliance on lumber, pulp and the US market. (The Globe and Mail, BNN Bloomberg (The Canadian Press))

item.title: SpaceX and Elon Musk pledge two shares to every active Trump Account, a gift valued at nearly $18 billion
item.description: SpaceX will issue one new share to every active Trump Account and Elon Musk will match it from his own holdings, a pledge worth nearly $18 billion at Wednesday's share price. (The Globe and Mail (Reuters), Fortune)

item.title: Beyond the First Best: Welfare and OPEC Market Power
item.description: A new framework for measuring cartel harm puts OPEC's cost to the world since 1970 at $2.2 trillion by the usual method, but about $0.7 trillion once other oil-market distortions are accounted for. (John Asker, Allan Collard-Wexler, Charlotte De Cannière et al.)

item.title: OpenAI countersues Apple, alleging trade-secret theft and pressure on suppliers of its planned AI devices
item.description: OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple in California federal court, accusing it of taking OpenAI hardware secrets through a rehired employee and of pressuring suppliers not to work on OpenAI's devices. (CNN, Reuters (via KFGO), AppleInsider)

item.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
item.description: TT-RSI lets a model re-solve unlabeled test questions with its own previous solution in view, then distills those refinements into its weights, beating majority-vote self-training on competition mathematics. (Jianyu Wu, Yizhou Wang, Encheng Su et al. · Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory)

item.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
item.description: On a benchmark built to test video generators as visual reasoners, coding agents that write a program to render the answer video score about 0.9 against 0.67 for the best video model. (Dezhi Luo, Fengyuan Yu, Haotian Zhang et al. · University College London, Nanyang Technological University, Carnegie Mellon University)

item.title: iWAM: Efficient Action Prediction from World Models without Explicit Future Prediction
item.description: iWAM conditions a robot policy on features from a single pass of a video model instead of a fully generated future, keeping the generalization of world-action models at much lower inference cost. (Vansh Kapoor, Max Sobol Mark, Sreyas Venkataraman et al. · Carnegie Mellon University)

item.title: RoboUniverse-10K: Toward the Scaling Era of Agentic Robotics via Real-to-Sim Environments
item.description: RoboUniverse-10K turns real robot videos into 10,807 verifiable simulation tasks for coding agents that control robots, and shows a split between frontier models near 86% and most others under 10%. (Jinkun Liu, Yingze Wang, Situ Wang et al. · Tsinghua University)

item.title: Improving and Expanding Video Editing Capabilities Without Videos
item.description: I2VT teaches video editors new kinds of edits using only single images, by having the video model edit one-frame videos while an image editor corrects every denoising step. (Ji Xie, Yanhao Jia, Xiangpeng Yang et al. · Carnegie Mellon University, Nanyang Technological University, University of Technology Sydney)

item.title: Hackers reportedly breach Cloud One, the US Air Force's main cloud platform, halting updates and migrations
item.description: Reuters reports that hackers exploited a software flaw to reach the control layer of Cloud One, the Air Force's cloud platform; the attackers and any data loss are unknown. (BleepingComputer, Engadget)

item.title: An unpatched flaw in the Cacti network monitoring tool is published with working attack code and no warning to developers
item.description: A researcher published a working exploit for an unpatched Cacti flaw that lets outsiders run commands when guest access is on; administrators should disable the guest account. (BleepingComputer, The Hacker News)

item.title: FIFA confirms a cyberattack exposed personal and business information after a new group claimed to leak 12 GB of files
item.description: FIFA says hackers accessed a "limited set of personal and business information"; a group called the Handsome Boy Hacking Club claims it took more than 12 GB of internal files. (SecurityWeek (AP), Infosecurity Magazine)

item.title: Microsoft issues an emergency fix after its November no-restart update crashes some Windows Server 2025 machines
item.description: Microsoft released an out-of-band update, KB5138318, for Windows Server 2025 machines that could crash when an IPv6 route expired after November's hotpatch. (The Register, BleepingComputer)

item.title: "More Than You Expect!": Leakage-Abuse Attacks on Encrypted Vector Search
item.description: Encrypted vector databases that reveal which records are returned together leak the records' topics: an attack called SAGE recovers category labels with up to 84.3% accuracy. (Yang Zhang, Ruiqi He, Xiaoqian Sun et al. · Nankai University)

item.title: Health Canada warns of a very rare risk of sudden vision loss with semaglutide drugs
item.description: Health Canada's completed safety review found a possible link between prescription semaglutide and NAION, a form of sudden, usually permanent vision loss, and product labels will be updated. (Health Canada, CBC News via Radio Canada International, Global News)

item.title: Flu admissions in England jump almost 80% in a week, the highest for late November since before Covid
item.description: Hospital admissions for flu in England rose from five to nearly nine per 100,000 people in a week, the highest for this point in November this decade, with vaccination lagging. (BBC News, The Guardian)

item.title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
item.description: An engineered protein glue called TALhesin held chromosome halves together in aged mouse eggs, raising the share of error-free eggs from 46.7% to 74.1%, close to the level in young mice. (Alexandre Webster, Halima Yusuf, Nina Schweizer et al. · Max Planck Institute for Multidisciplinary Sciences, Göttingen; eggs donated via Göttingen Fertility Center, Bourn Hall Fertility Clinic (Cambridgeshire) and Fertility Center Berlin)

item.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
item.description: Structures of a CRISPR-associated transposase revealed how it locks onto a precise genomic target, and redesigned proteins made it 100 times more active without losing on-target specificity. (Shirin Fatma, Shubham Dubey, Vinh H. Truong et al. · St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, Department of Structural Biology)

item.title: In vivo genome-editing therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy: Preclinical studies and first-in-human trial
item.description: A single-dose CRISPR therapy delivered by one AAV9 vector produced the first molecular evidence of gene editing in the muscles of boys with Duchenne muscular dystrophy, but one of four participants died. (Guoling Li, Feng Han, Cuijin Wang et al. · HuidaGene Therapeutics (Shanghai), Chinese Academy of Sciences, Shanghai Jiao Tong University)

item.title: Peatlands drained since 1800 account for about 2.7% of human-caused warming, and the effect could nearly double by 2100
item.description: An MIT-led study in Nature estimates that draining about 15% of the world's peatlands has caused roughly 2.7% of human-driven warming, with emissions set to continue for centuries. (MIT News, Ars Technica)

item.title: MIT team reports signatures of paraparticles, a third kind of particle statistics, in a lattice of superconducting qubits
item.description: Using 16 superconducting qubits, MIT researchers built excitations that pass three tests for paraparticles, objects that follow neither the boson nor the fermion rulebook. (New Scientist, arXiv)

item.title: A US judge finds a second planned seabed-mining lease sale, off the Northern Mariana Islands, violated the Endangered Species Act
item.description: A federal judge ruled that the wildlife review behind a 16 December seabed-mining lease sale off the Northern Mariana Islands ignored the mining the leases could eventually allow. (BBC, Earthjustice)

item.title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
item.description: River flow and lake and reservoir storage fell together worldwide in 2023 and 2024, the largest drop since 1991, with South America responsible for about 70% of the lost streamflow. (Pedro L. B. Chaffe, Georgia Destouni, Francis H. S. Chiew et al.)

item.title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
item.description: The magnitude 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake of 2025 appears to have started in a rough part of the fault, a kind of zone usually thought to stop giant ruptures, before breaking into a smoother one. (Haipeng Luo, Fengzhou Tan, Zhangfeng Ma et al.)

item.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
item.description: A plasma process melts cement ingredients and forms clinker in seconds instead of hours, using electricity in place of fossil-fuelled kilns. (Qi Zheng, Haiyan Mao, Chengyao Liang et al.)

item.title: Euro zone countries pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president
item.description: Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, was chosen to lead the European Central Bank from February, with inflation at 4% and a December rate rise widely expected. (The Globe and Mail, CRBC News)

item.title: Chinese stocks post their biggest gains in two years after Beijing promises a larger role for state-backed buyers
item.description: The CSI 300 rose 4.2% and a chip index jumped a record 19% after China's cabinet said state-backed investors would do more to stabilise a market at 17-month lows. (Reuters (via WIFC), Oninvest)

item.title: Trump calls pre-election GDP figures "fake" and demands an investigation after a routine upward revision
item.description: President Trump alleged, without evidence, that officials deliberately understated third-quarter growth before the midterm elections, after a scheduled revision lifted it from 3.4% to 4.3%. (Fortune, Bloomberg (via The Spokesman-Review), Fox Business)

item.title: Fed's Beige Book finds slight to moderate growth in eight districts, with wage gains picking up and costs outpacing prices
item.description: The Federal Reserve's regional survey shows a slowly growing economy in which consumers are price sensitive, housing and construction are weakening and wage growth has stepped up to a moderate pace. (Federal Reserve, Federal Reserve)

item.title: AI, Automation, and Fiscal Pressure
item.description: A model calibrated to the EU finds that AI-driven automation can widen budget deficits even as it grows the economy, because income shifts from heavily taxed labor to lightly taxed capital. (Spencer Bastani, Georg Graetz, Bernat Pla et al.)

item.title: OpenAI says its GPT-6 models design binding proteins without specialized biology models
item.description: OpenAI reports that GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences using reasoning and code alone, with 35 of 322 lab-made minibinders binding their intended targets across five targets. (OpenAI)

item.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
item.description: The authors trace long-context training crashes in Gated DeltaNet-2 to an asymmetric erase operation that inflates the recurrent state, and fix it by making erasure symmetric. (Xichong Zhang, Xixuan Hao, Zhichen Liu et al. · MemTensor)

item.title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
item.description: A small reasoning model can absorb a stronger teacher's agent policy from the teacher's actions alone, with its own reasoning block left empty during training, and still think at inference. (Dawid J. Kopiczko, Tijmen Blankevoort, Yuki M. Asano · University of Technology Nuremberg, NVIDIA)

item.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
item.description: Letting models decide when and what to compact in their own context beats harness-triggered compaction at tight budgets, but only for models that actually use the interface. (Alessio Devoto, Avinash Vem, Tara Safavi et al. · NVIDIA)

item.title: Agentic LongLive: Asynchronous Agentic Memory for Long Video Generation
item.description: A memory agent running on separate GPUs prepares text and image memory for the next shot before its prompt arrives, giving a real-time video generator long-term consistency at about 1% extra time. (Shaoteng Liu, Shuai Yang, Wei Huang et al. · NVIDIA, MIT, CUHK)

item.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
item.description: Putting a mirror in the scene cuts success rates of five generalist robot policies by 10.8 to 56.7 percentage points, and most failures happen without the robot ever touching the mirror. (Xuanchen Liu, Hejun Zhang, Boxuan Dong et al. · Peking University)

item.title: A 12-year-old flaw in the Linux kernel's NFS file server lets remote attackers gain root without logging in
item.description: Security firm OpenSec detailed NFS2ROOT, a critical flaw present in Linux's built-in NFS server since 2014 that lets an unauthenticated attacker who can reach port 2049 take full control. (OpenSec, BleepingComputer)

item.title: Britain's Department for Work and Pensions takes online services offline after a cyber incident
item.description: The UK department that pays the state pension and benefits said it took some online services offline as a precaution after a cyber incident, and that regular payments are not affected. (The Record, The Register)

item.title: SAP confirms suspicious activity in its systems after Der Spiegel reports attackers altered its source code on GitHub
item.description: SAP says it found suspicious activity and sees no evidence that customer business data was accessed; Der Spiegel reports that attackers stole employees' GitHub tokens and copied and modified source code. (BleepingComputer, t-online, Security Affairs)

item.title: Google will publish the phone numbers and addresses of money-making Android developers worldwide from March 2027
item.description: To comply with EU and UK rules, Google will show a phone number and address for every Play Store developer classed as a trader, visible to users everywhere and with no PO boxes allowed. (The Verge, Engadget)

item.title: The first generic version of the twice-yearly HIV prevention shot lenacapavir arrives in Zambia, at about $40 a year
item.description: The Global Fund says the first generic lenacapavir, a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection expected to cost about $40 per person a year, has reached Zambia, with Uganda next. (The Global Fund, BBC, Associated Press (via Yahoo News))

item.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 12,000 confirmed cases, with only 15% of new cases among known contacts
item.description: Government data show more than 12,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, and most new cases are still appearing outside known chains of transmission. (US CDC, ECDC, Reuters (via Head Topics))

item.title: Hepatitis B vaccination at birth falls to 65.6% of US newborns, and slips among babies of infected mothers, a records study finds
item.description: An analysis of health records for 1.3 million US infants finds hepatitis B vaccination within a day of birth fell from about 80% in 2022 to 65.6% by June 2026. (Truveta, NEJM Evidence)

item.title: Blood-Pressure–Lowering Treatment across the Cardiovascular Risk Spectrum
item.description: Pooling 51 randomized trials and 357,440 people, blood-pressure drugs cut major cardiovascular events by the same relative amount at every level of predicted risk, but the absolute gain shrinks as risk falls. (Zeinab Bidel Milad Nazarzadeh Borislava Mihaylova Qianqian Yang Johan Sundström Nathalie Conrad Dexter Canoy Guyu Zeng David M. Kent William C. Cushman John Chalmers Koon K. Teo Carl J. Pepine Barry R. Davis Mark Woodward and Kazem Rahimithe Blood Pressure Lowering Treatment Trialists’ Collaboration*)

item.title: Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
item.description: Across about 219,000 people in five long-running studies, later-born generations enter old age with better memory and lose it more slowly. (Anders Fjell et al. · University of Oslo)

item.title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
item.description: Enamel proteins from four teeth found in two caves in Guangxi point to two kinds of archaic human in southern China: one Denisovan-like, one that fits no sampled group. (Song Xing, Huiyun Rao, Guangmao Xie et al. · Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology, Beijing)

item.title: Hera's first close-ups show DART left a stadium-sized crater and a tumbling asteroid surrounded by boulders
item.description: ESA's Hera spacecraft has returned the first close images of Dimorphos, showing that NASA's 2022 DART impact carved a crater nearly as wide as the asteroid and left it tumbling. (CNN, Ars Technica)

item.title: Niobium phosphide wires a few nanometres wide conduct better as they shrink, the opposite of copper
item.description: A Stanford-led study in Nature reports that ribbons of the semimetal niobium phosphide only 5 to 6 nanometres wide become less resistive as they narrow, unlike copper chip wiring. (Tech Xplore (Stanford University release), Nature)

item.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
item.description: Draining peatlands since 1800 accounts for about 2.7% of today's human-caused warming influence, and the effect could nearly double by 2100 even if no more peatland is drained. (Jevan B. Yu, Etienne Fluet-Chouinard, Susan E. Page et al. · Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Pacific Northwest National Laboratory; University of Leicester; UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology)

item.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
item.description: Delft physicists coupled two minimal Kitaev chains in a nanowire and observed coherent oscillations of fermion parity, which they describe as the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit. (Francesco Zatelli, Bart Roovers, Nick van Loo et al. · Delft University of Technology)

item.title: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other trading partners over excess factory capacity
item.description: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs on 14 economies, including an additional 20% on Chinese goods, to replace import taxes the Supreme Court struck down in February. (The Globe and Mail, BBC, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US PCE inflation holds at 3.8% in October and core inflation reaches 3.3%, as real consumer spending slips
item.description: The Federal Reserve's preferred price index rose 3.8% in the year to October, and 3.3% excluding food and energy, slightly above the 3.2% core rate economists expected. (Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US third-quarter GDP growth is revised up to 4.3%, the fastest pace in three years
item.description: The US economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, not 3.4% as first estimated, after upgrades to software investment and consumer spending. (Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Norse Atlantic suspends its flights and says it will file for bankruptcy unless it finds funding urgently
item.description: The Norwegian long-haul budget airline cancelled Thursday's flights a day after its shares fell 85%, and says it is in takeover talks with investors. (RTE, Euronews)

item.title: UK discount chain Poundland collapses into administration, putting 11,000 jobs and 600 shops at risk
item.description: Poundland's US owner, Gordon Brothers, put the retailer into administration after sale talks failed; shops stay open while administrators AlixPartners seek buyers for all or parts of it. (BBC, Euronews, BBC)

item.title: Democratizing Venture Capital: Tax Incentives and the Geographic Expansion of Startup Investing
item.description: Removing federal capital gains tax on qualifying startup stock in 2009–2010 raised the chance that a metro area with no venture capital received its first investment by 8 to 10 percentage points. (Murillo Campello, Guilherme Junqueira)

item.title: Nvidia reportedly halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries after new US chip export rule
item.description: The Financial Times reports that Nvidia told server makers to stop shipping to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after a US rule made advanced-chip exports to those countries subject to licences. (The Star (Reuters), Al Jazeera)
